extracted.intended_audience: postdoctoral researchers preparing NIMH NIH K99/R00 (Pathway to Independence) applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing an NIH Pathway to Independence (K99/R00) application to NIMH, eligibility for the K99 and R00 phases, and rules for transitioning to the independent (R00) phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: PD/PI eligibility — postdoctoral experience limit
rubrics_metrics.description: K99/R00 applicants must have no more than 4 years of postdoctoral research experience at the time of application regardless of whether it is a new or resubmission application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Postdoctoral research is defined as any time spent conducting research or publishing research results following completion of all degree requirements, which may not correspond with the date of the graduation ceremony. This includes any time spent at the institution where the doctoral degree was completed prior to starting an official postdoctoral position. Applicants are strongly encouraged to apply as soon as they have developed a conceptual framework and preliminary data; it is not recommended to wait until the end of the eligibility window if a candidate is otherwise strong.

rubrics_metrics.name: PD/PI eligibility — must be in mentored postdoctoral position
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must be in mentored, postdoctoral training positions to be eligible to apply to the K99/R00 program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given that the K99 phase is intended for mentored career development, a well-justified and feasible set of mentored career development goals for the K99 phase that complements the applicant’s current skill set is expected. Applications lacking a well-reasoned set of mentored career development goals generally do not receive favorable reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence before award — disqualification
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant achieves independence (any faculty or non-mentored research position) before a K99 award is made, neither the K99, nor the R00 award, will be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The K99 phase is specifically for mentored career development; having independent status prior to award removes eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship and visa status
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no citizenship requirement for K99 applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant may be a U.S. citizen, non-citizen national, permanent resident, or a non-U.S. citizen. For applicants on temporary U.S. visas, visa status during each phase of the K99/R00 award must allow the PD/PI to conduct the proposed research at the applicant institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible institutions are U.S. domestic institutions; foreign components are allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should confirm institutional eligibility and any institutional requirements related to grant administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentored career development plan quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The K99 phase requires a well-justified and feasible set of mentored career development goals that complement the applicant’s current skill set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications lacking a well-reasoned set of mentored career development goals generally do not receive favorable reviews. The K99 phase is intended for mentored career development, so the plan should clearly articulate how mentored training will prepare the applicant for independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum mentored training duration under K99
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees are expected to complete at least one full year of mentored training under the K99 phase before transitioning to the R00 phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This expectation supports the intent of the K99 as a mentored development stage prior to independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition to R00 — required position and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: To activate the independent phase of the grant, individuals must have been offered and accepted a tenure-track, full-time assistant professor position (or equivalent) by the end of the K99 project period. The faculty position may not be contingent upon receipt of an R00 award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transition from K99 to R00 is not automatic and is subject to NIMH administrative review of the K99 awardee’s accomplishments and the materials submitted in support of the R00 phase (including the faculty job offer). K99 awardees are strongly encouraged to contact their Program Officer as they begin to interview for tenure-track positions and to provide regular status updates. K99 awardees should notify their Program Officer upon receipt of any tenure-track job offer (and prior to acceptance) so the PO may address questions concerning expectations for transition to R00.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition administrative timing and review
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals should allow three months for NIMH review of R00 phase applications. R00 applications submitted after July 15 annually will generally not be reviewed until the next fiscal year (after October 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan job searches and submission timing accordingly; late submissions may delay review into the next fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: R00 phase duration and contingency
rubrics_metrics.description: The R00 phase provides up to 3 years of independent research support, which is contingent on satisfactory progress during the K99 phase and an approved, independent, tenure-track (or equivalent) faculty position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The two award phases are intended to be continuous in time, but activation of R00 requires satisfactory administrative review and meeting the position eligibility criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: R00 expectations — pursue independent R01 support
rubrics_metrics.description: Award recipients are expected to apply for independent R01 support from the NIMH during the R00 award period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The R00 is intended to bridge to independent, competitive NIH funding; awardees should plan for timely R01 submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary and research support limits — K99 phase
rubrics_metrics.description: K99 phase salary support: Up to $75,000 plus fringe benefits per year. Practicing physician-scientists may be eligible for up to $100,000 salary plus fringe benefits per year. Research support: Up to $20,000 per year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requested salary must be consistent with the institution's established salary structure and salaries for comparable staff, and must not exceed the legislatively mandated salary cap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary and total costs — R00 phase
rubrics_metrics.description: The total cost for the independent phase (R00) may not exceed $249,000. This amount includes salary, fringe benefits, research costs, and applicable indirect costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When budgeting, include all applicable costs within this cap and ensure salary requests align with institutional norms and the NIH salary cap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application assignment — study section
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should not request a specific study section for their K99/R00 application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All NIMH K99/R00 applications are assigned to an NIMH study section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver process for 4-year eligibility window
rubrics_metrics.description: NIMH will grant an eligibility waiver on a case-by-case basis for the 4-year postdoctoral limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions may be considered when a significant break in training occurred due to family responsibilities, medical leave, or military service, or when there was a significant change in fields of study (e.g., moving from physical science to life science research). Investigators are expected to contact NIMH staff to discuss eligibility prior to applying and to learn if their circumstance warrants an exception (see K Award Eligibility Extension page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and communication with Program Officer
rubrics_metrics.description: K99 awardees are strongly encouraged to contact their Program Officer as they begin to interview for tenure-track faculty positions and to provide regular status updates on their job search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such communication allows staff to provide technical assistance during the job search and negotiation; awardees are expected to notify their PO upon receipt of any tenure-track job offer (and prior to acceptance) so questions about NIMH expectations for R00 transition can be addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of postdoctoral research
rubrics_metrics.description: Postdoctoral research is any time spent conducting research or publishing research results following completion of all degree requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition may not correspond with the date of the graduation ceremony and includes time spent at the institution where the doctoral degree was completed prior to starting an official postdoctoral position.
